## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first 2D game about assembling heroes in a minecart, descending into caves, deploying them, fighting enemies, earning coins, and upgrading the cart and roster.

## Requirements
- No scrolling webpages; the game should be designed specifically for mobile.
- Start with one available cart slot; allow buying more slots.
- Include a shop with randomized hero chest rewards and a chest-opening animation.
- Enemies get harder as the player progresses; defeating them earns coins.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with local save data and touch-friendly controls.
- Added a camp ledger, hero stats, battle skills, escalating cave depths, and offline SVG artwork to round out gameplay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented surface, shop, cave deployment, animated battles, results, upgrades, hero recruitment, and save persistence.
- Mobile browser checks exercised shop, slot purchase, cave deployment, and battle on a seeded save.
- `node --check` succeeded for `js/game.js`, `js/data.js`, and `js/art.js`.

### Active
- Final review of the battle/result flow; a seeded battle verification was run and produced `screenshots/check-result.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/check-result.jpg` and relevant battle code for any final visual or gameplay issues.
2. Run any needed final checks and summarize the completed implementation to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game entry page and script loading.
- `styles.css`: Mobile-first layout, screens, animations, and game styling.
- `js/data.js`: Heroes, enemies, progression data, and SVG portraits.
- `js/art.js`: Scene and chest artwork.
- `js/game.js`: Game state, rendering, controls, shop, combat, and persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.
- Local development server was started on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Seeded verification screenshots are in `screenshots/`, including `screenshots/check-result.jpg`; these are test artifacts, not necessarily part of the desired deliverable.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

The game seems complete. I want to verify in a browser after any changes. Before that, let me review potential quality issues:

1. Balance: default 35 coins, chest 55. Slot cost 80. First run at depth 1: one hero pip (12 atk, 138 hp) vs 1 bat (46*0.78=36 hp, atk 4.8*0.82≈4). Easily wins. Reward ~ 12*0.8=10 + clear 16 = 26, plus XP. First run earns 26 coins; starting 35 → 61, enough for chest after run. Good.

2. Battle difficulty scaling: depthHp 1.3^(d-1) and enemy count 1+floor((d-1)/2). At depth 10: 1.3^9 = 10.6, count 5 capped 4? count = min(4, 1+floor(9/2)=5) = 4. Boss wraith at depth 10: 46*10.6*1.5*partyScale. With 5 heroes partyScale=1.56 → 1140 hp boss. Heroes at level ~? XP per run 17+5d. Might be okay.

3. Potential bug: in `finishBattle`, `battle.coinsEarned` includes coins for kills; boss bonus added after floating coin. Fine.

4. On defeat, state.depth stays, and crew "fully healed" since next battle recreates heroes at full hp. Good.

5. Bug: `showBattleResult` calls `battle?.enemies.some` after finishBattle; battle is still set. Fine.

6. The "result" overlay adds to overlayRoot; while overlay open, stage still battle. Click on hero could cast skill because battle.over true so no effect. Fine.

7. `renderSurface` slot click handlers: when slot filled, index maps to cart; fine.

8. `state.cart` might contain heroes beyond slots if slots decreased? never decreases.

9. `openShop` re-renders overlay after buying slot, requiring user opening chest? fine.

10. Shop chest button disabled when no locked heroes, so no coin cache purchases. Text says "the chest now holds a coin cache" but button disabled 'Complete'—inconsistency. Actually chooseChestReward supports coins when all heroes owned, but buy button is disabled when no lockedHeroes. So the coin-cache fallback never triggers from shop. It's not a bug per se, but text "Your crew is complete. The chest now holds a coin cache." followed by disabled "Complete" is contradictory. Since all 8 heroes owned is endgame. Better to allow infinite chest coin purchases? Or change text to "Your crew is complete — every hero is already at camp." Let me fix copy. But is it important? Minor polish.

11. There's a bug in `bindBackdropClose`: showOverlay wraps in `.overlay`; for full-bleed overlays (chest/result) it doesn't add overlay wrapper. `openShop`: `$('.overlay')` is fine.

12. Chest overlay: clicking backdrop doesn't close (intended). After reveal, "Meet the crew" closes and returns shop. Fine. But if player buys chest and doesn't tap open, the chest overlay is stuck? It requires tap to open; there's no close button. They can use browser back? No. The overlay blocks everything. Since tapping the chest stage opens, that's fine, but user might want to skip. Maybe okay.

13. Escape handler only knows shopClose or helpClose, not chest. Fine.

14. `openChestOverlay` opens with `showOverlay` full-bleed regex: `/^<div class="(?:chest-overlay|result-overlay)/` — but the HTML string starts with newline and spaces then `<div class="chest-overlay"...`. `html.trim()` strips leading whitespace. Good.

15. The `overlayRoot` has class open; clicking outside chest-overlay might not close. Fine.

16. A11y: fine.

17. Mobile view tests: need to check at 390x844. Existing screenshots indicate good.

The final screenshot check-result shows the result overlay with "COINS HAULED 54" and "CREW XP +96". Looks good, though XP +96 seems huge relative to base 17+depth*5 = 22 at depth 1 for one hero. Wait the screenshot maybe depth 6. Fine.

Potential visual bug in seed-surface screenshot: the cart card overlapped the scene; actually layout uses fixed stage and scrolls internally? Requirement "no scrolling webpages"; the surface appears scrollable? In the screenshot, the content below the fold maybe. Let's look at CSS and at a fresh screenshot. We need to check if the page scrolls. The requirement is no scrolling webpages; but mobile game can have internal scrolling? They wanted no scrolling webpages, presumably fit. On 390x844, surface screenshot showed all content from header to actions? Let me open image again to inspect. It was removed from context, but I can re-read with tool. Actually the display says "older screenshot removed to save context; take a new one if needed". I can take new screenshots. Let me run the game and use playwright-cli.

**Down-Bound is complete and verified.** The final session was spent hunting down and fixing the last visual defect: on shorter browser viewports (the common case on real phones, e.g. 390×664), the hero cards and camp ledger were clipped off-screen, and the "Depth N awaits" badge sat unreadably over the sun. All fixed and re-verified across five viewport classes.

## What was finished in this pass
- **Short-viewport fit fix** — added compact layout tiers at ≤840px, ≤700px, ≤620px and ≤520px heights, plus a combined query so short desktop windows (≤900px) fit too. Verified zero overflow (content height == container height) at 320×568, 390×664, 1280×830/844 and 1280×910.
- **Badge legibility** — the surface "Camp awake / Depth awaits" pill now has a translucent blurred backdrop instead of floating over the sun.
- **Seat label** — "SEAT 1" moved inside the empty slot instead of colliding with the rail.
- **Favicon** — inline SVG pickaxe icon; console now shows **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- **Endgame chest** — the hero chest stays purchasable after the full 8-hero roster, paying out a coin cache instead of a duplicate (verified: bought at 115, received +84 coins).
- **Balance semantics** — "Best depth" now records the deepest *cleared* depth; skill-name floaters clamp to the arena width on narrow screens.

## Verified end-to-end on a live browser
Fresh save → load Pip → descend → deploy → fight → victory (+28 coins, Depth 2 charted) → surface; seeded multi-hero cave deployment, battle with special casts, victory and defeat result screens; chest open animation and coin reveal; shop purchases; full 5-seat cart at 320px width; help and reset flows. Screenshots for each step are in `screenshots/` (git-ignored test artifacts).

## How to play
1. **Surface** — tap a crew member to load the minecart (one seat to start), then **Descend**.
2. **Cave** — tap a cart hero, then a glowing pad (or drag them down), then **Fight**.
3. **Battle** — auto-attacks run; tap any deployed hero to unleash their special when the ring fills.
4. **Spend** — kills and clears pay coins; the Trading Post sells random hero chests (82% recruit chance, with an open animation) and +1 cart seats up to 5 seats. Enemies scale up every depth; every victory charts the next one.

Files: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/data.js`, `js/art.js`, `js/game.js` — all plain HTML/CSS/JS with localStorage saves, no page scrolling, portrait-mobile-first. Both changes are committed (`b7f3af3`, `fae364c`), and a dev server is still running at `http://localhost:3002` if you want to play it now.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first 2D game about assembling heroes in a minecart, exploring caves, fighting enemies, earning coins, and upgrading the cart and roster.

## Requirements
- No scrolling webpages; design specifically for mobile.
- Start with one available cart slot and allow buying more.
- Include a shop with randomized hero chest rewards and a chest-opening animation.
- Increase enemy difficulty with progression and award coins for defeating enemies.

## Decisions
- Implemented as standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with local saves and touch-friendly controls.
- Added a camp ledger, hero stats and skills, escalating cave depths, offline SVG artwork, and coin-cache rewards after recruiting all heroes.

## Work State
### Completed

- Fixed compact-viewport layout, surface badge contrast, seat label placement, favicon, skill-label bounds, and best-depth tracking.
- Verified fresh-save and seeded gameplay flows, shop/chest rewards, reset/help flows, and responsive layouts from 320×568 through desktop sizes; browser console reported no errors or warnings.

- `index.html`: Game entry page, script loading, and inline SVG favicon.

- `js/data.js`: Heroes, enemies, progression data, and SVG portraits.

The user wants three things:

1. **Revamp the hero bubble portraits** using the full-body battle sprite models as reference. The bubbles currently "look bad" — they're the old portrait SVG (64x64 portrait art). They want the cool full-body models reflected in the bubbles.

2. **Improve enemy models a lot** — they look bad.

3. **Combat movement change**: characters shouldn't "jump to attack and jump back" (walk out, strike, return to formation) making it look turn-based. Instead, when the fight starts they should fight in real time — meaning they should move fluidly around the arena, engaging continuously rather than returning to home positions after each attack. Like a real-time brawl where units move around the battlefield continuously.

Let me think about what "fight in real time" means concretely:
- Units should leave formation at fight start and engage — no static home positions to return to.
- Melee units move toward targets, attack when in range, and stay engaged; if their target dies, they pick a new target and move to it.
- Avoid the "walk out → strike → walk back" loop. Instead: continuous movement, attack when within range, coalesce into a melee scrum, reposition when targets die or new ones appear.
- Maybe add idle bobbing, facing direction, circling/dodging movement to make it look alive.

Let me plan the implementation:

### A. Hero bubble portraits revamp

Current `portraitSvg(hero)` draws 64x64 portrait art per hero (used in `.portrait` bubbles). The battle sprites are 64x80 full-body. The cleanest approach: make the bubble portraits render the full-body sprite scaled/cropped to a head-and-torso portrait? Or simply use the full-body sprite inside the bubble (whole character visible in the circle)? The user says "use their models there and make them into bubbles... use the cool models of the heros as reference to revamp the bubbles".

Interpretation: replace the bubble portrait art with the battle models — i.e., show the full-body characters inside the circular bubbles. But a full-body 64x80 in a circle needs scaling to fit the height — the character would be small. Alternatively, zoom/crop to show upper body (head + torso + weapon) from the battle sprite. That would look consistent and cool.

Best approach: in `portraitSvg(hero)`, render the `heroSpriteSvg(hero)` art inside a viewBox that crops the upper portion: e.g., viewBox "8 4 48 48" showing head + torso + some weapon. But the battle sprites have specific compositions (weapons at edges); cropping to 48x48 centered on the head (x 12-52, y ~2-46) would show head + torso. Let me think: heads are around y 10-32; torso 30-56. A crop y 2-50, x 6-58 shows head + upper torso + props at shoulder height (pickaxe head top-right, bow, staff crystal, bomb). That's a decent portrait.

Bubble is circular; the `.portrait` element isn't clipped circularly? Check CSS: `.portrait` used in hero cards with border-radius? The `.hero-card .portrait`... The bubble is likely a rounded square/circle with the portrait SVG filling. Let me check `.portrait` CSS. Earlier I saw `.unit-portrait .portrait` (removed). For hero cards: `.hero-card .portrait` etc. Need to look.

Option B: Keep `portraitSvg` function but rebuild each current portrait art to match the new models (colors/props consistent) — that's redundant. Better to derive the portrait from the battle sprite directly: `portraitSvg(hero)` returns `<svg viewBox="6 2 52 52">` + heroSprite art. Since the sprite art strings are defined inside heroSpriteSvg, refactor: extract `HERO_SPRITE_ART` map (module-level), then:
- `heroSpriteSvg(hero)` → full 64x80.
- `portraitSvg(hero)` → same art with a zoomed viewBox.

This guarantees visual consistency. Risk: the crop might cut weapons oddly, and the circular mask (if any) might clip. Test with screenshots.

Also the chest reveal uses `.reveal-portrait` with portraitSvg — will also get the new look, consistent.

Also mini enemy stack on surface uses enemySvg — improved enemy art will flow there automatically.

### B. Enemy model improvements

Current enemy art: bat, slime, goblin, skeleton, spider, golem, wraith — simple flat shapes, 64x64. The user says they look bad. I need to substantially rework these seven enemies with better shading, anatomy, details — keeping 64x64 viewBox (used in mini-foe stack and battle). Make them bigger/detailed like the heroes: outlines, depth, highlights, expressive eyes.

Let me design each with more detail:

1. **Cave Bat** (flying, dark purple): body with fur texture strokes, large membrane wings with rib lines, big ears, glowing red eyes, fangs. Add gradients? The hero sprites use flat fills with darker shading shapes — no gradients (no defs). For enemies I can use flat shading too. Make wings larger with scalloped edges.

2. **Moss Slime** (green blob): glossy body with layered jelly, bubbles inside, moss/leaves on top, big expressive eyes, drips, puddle shadow.

3. **Cave Goblin**: green skin, big hooked nose, pointy ears, leather vest, crude dagger/club, belt, uneven teeth, red eyes.

4. **Lost Miner** (skeleton): skull with miner helmet + lamp (candle?), ribcage, arm bones, rusty pickaxe, tattered clothes.

5. **Silkfang** (spider): big abdomen with markings, eight jointed legs with segments, multiple eyes cluster, fangs, web strands.

6. **Gloom Golem** (boss): hulking rock body with cracks glowing orange, crystal shards on shoulders, heavy fists, small glowing eyes, moss.

7. **Vein Wraith** (boss): floating tattered cloak, teal ghost fire, skeletal hands, glowing core, wispy tail, hooded void face.

Each need to stay readable at ~42-56px (battle) and ~20px (mini stack). Bold silhouettes.

### C. Real-time combat (no jump-attack-return)

Redesign the movement AI:

- At fight start (after `battle.delay`), melee units leave formations and engage. Currently each attack triggers a walk out + strike + walk home. Instead:
  - Units continuously move: each unit has a target; they approach until within `range` (adjacent offset), then stop and attack on their timer while standing engaged.
  - After attacking, they DON'T walk home. They stay engaged (maybe small bob/dodge).
  - When their target dies, they re-acquire the nearest living enemy and move there.
  - Ranged units reposition slightly between shots (strafe), maybe drift.
  - To prevent everyone stacking into one blob at the same spot, keep per-unit offsets around the target (angle-based: assign each attacker a slot around the target).

This makes it feel like a continuous melee scramble.

Implementation plan:

State per unit:
- `tx, ty` current target position (not home).
- `engaged` target unit (or null).
- `range` (melee 7-8% x offset).

Approach A (simplest robust): in battleTick, for each living melee unit:
1. If no combat target or target dead → pick a living opposing unit (nearest).
2. Compute desired stand point near target: base offset = ±(6-9)% in x, plus small per-unit lateral offset to spread attackers: use unit.slot angle around target.
3. Move toward the stand point at walk speed (continuous, every frame). When within ~1.5% of stand point → "in range": stop moving, attack on timer cadence.
4. Attack timer only ticks when in range (so approach time doesn't bank attacks). On attack: lunge animation + damage, no walk away.
5. Ranged units: stay at range distance (e.g., 22-30% away), drift to maintain distance if enemies approach? Keep simple: ranged units pick a stand point at distance ~25% from target, move there, shoot on timer. They still “kite” if target comes close? Not necessary.

For enemies: same logic mirrored. Melee enemies approach heroes; ranged stay back.

Formation at start: units begin at their formation spots, then immediately begin moving to engage once battle.delay ends — so the fight starts with a charge, then continuous brawling. 

Also visually: while walking, walk-bob animation (already exists). While engaged and attacking: lunge-right/left animation already used. The units never return to home, so no more "jump back".

Target clustering: multiple units engaging the same target need distinct stand points. Compute per-attacker angle slots: e.g., for the k-th attacker of target (attackerIndex among all living attackers assigned to that target), offset angle = spread. Simpler: use attacker's slot index to offset Y by (slot - (n-1)/2) * 8% and x by ±7. Since arena is 2.5D, front/back rows make sense: melee attackers array around target with y offset ±: e.g., 2 attackers: offsets (-7, -6), (-7, +6) in (dx, dy). 3+: spread across 3 positions on the near side.

Simplest deterministic: assign offset based on the attacker's own `slot` parity and index: 
```js
const lane = (unit.slot % 4); // 0..3
const offsets = [[-8, -7], [-9, 5], [-7, 12], [-11, -14]]; // relative dx from target, dy
```
Hmm, dx for heroes is negative (stand left of target), for enemies positive. dy spreads vertically. Use lane offsets from a table. Each attacker keeps its lane. If two units share a lane (slot mod 4 collision), acceptable overlap is rare since slots are unique (0..2 heroes, 0..3 enemies).

```js
function moveUnitToward(unit, x, y, dt) {
  const dx = x - unit.x, dy = y - unit.y;
  const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
  const speed = unit.boss ? 40 : 78;
  if (dist > 0.6) {
    const step = Math.min(dist, speed * dt);
    unit.x += dx / dist * step;
    unit.y += dy / dist * step;
    setMoving(unit, true);
  } else {
    setMoving(unit, false);
  }
  unit.el.style.setProperty('--x', ...);
  unit.el.style.setProperty('--y', ...);
  unit.engaged = dist < 2.5;
}
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve hero bubble portraits and enemy models, and convert battle combat from turn-based lunge attacks into continuous real-time fighting.

## Requirements
- Revamp bubble portraits using the existing cool full-body hero models as visual references.
- Significantly improve all enemy artwork.
- Keep full-body characters in battle.
- Make combat continuous and real-time, with characters pursuing and fighting rather than attacking and jumping back.
- Preserve smooth mobile-first gameplay and no flash or black-screen issues.

## Decisions
- Hero bubbles now reuse `HERO_SPRITE_ART` from the battle models through a bust-view SVG crop.
- Added detailed SVG artwork for bat, slime, goblin, skeleton, spider, golem, and wraith enemies.
- Replaced lunge-and-return movement with continuous pursuit, slot-paired dueling, ranged attacks, and melee engagements.
- Battle labels and health bars are moving to a separate arena-level overlay to prevent sprite overlap.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `HERO_SPRITE_ART` map and route hero bubble SVGs through it.
- Rebuilt all portrait and enemy SVG rendering in `js/data.js`.
- Replaced the battle movement and attack loop with real-time pursuit and cooldown-based attacks.
- Added continuous walking and melee strike animations without jump-to-target/return behavior.
- Added paired target acquisition and stable duel spots.
- Improved desktop, mobile, chest, deployment, and battle testing for runtime errors and transitions.
- Existing committed baseline remains recorded by commit `53bef32`.

### Active
- Final visual verification of battle labels, hero/enemy depth layering, and enemy readability.
- Verify the latest real-time combat implementation across victory, defeat, narrow-mobile, and desktop flows.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run a final browser test of fresh save, battle start, continuous combat, victory, defeat, chest rewards, and return flows.
2. Review screenshots for overlapping labels, hero/foe spacing, and enemy readability.
3. Commit the portrait, enemy, and real-time combat changes once final verification passes.

## Relevant Files
- `js/data.js`: Hero portrait crop source, battle hero sprite art, and redesigned enemy SVG art.
- `js/game.js`: Real-time combat pursuit, target acquisition, attacks, unit placement, and battle labels.
- `styles.css`: Battle strike/idle animations and unit-label/health-bar layout.
- `index.html`: Game entry and resource loading.

## Important Context
- New portrait and combat implementation work is expected to be uncommitted unless explicitly committed during the latest changes.
- The enemy list includes `bat`, `slime`, `goblin`, `skeleton`, `spider`, `golem`, and `wraith`.
- `portraitSvg()` intentionally uses `viewBox="7 1 50 50"` to crop battle models into bust portraits.
- The battle implementation must avoid old lunge animations and turn-based movement helpers.

## What changed in this final pass

**Pre-joined duels (`js/game.js`)**
- Every battle now starts *already in melee*: `pairFighters()` pre-places all melee fighters at their exact duel spots at battle start, so nobody charges in from the back line or bounces home after a swing.
